macos.query: SELECT value FROM credential WHERE integration_id = 'opencode-go' AND active = 1 ORDER BY time_created DESC, time_updated DESC LIMIT 1

fields.token: value is {"type":"key","key":"<key>"}: its key | apiKey | api_key | token | accessToken
$['opencode-go'] as string, or its key | apiKey | api_key | token | accessToken

macos.notes: opencode v2 writes logins to its SQLite store and no longer to auth.json. Replacing a key adds a row with active = 1 and sets the old row to active = 0, so the newest active row wins. auth.json (opencode v1) is read only when the database is missing or holds no active opencode-go row; a v1 file left behind holds whatever key was current when v2 took over. A store opencode holds busy is transient (credentialExpired), never a fallback to auth.json. Only opencode-go: every other integration (openai, google…) is that vendor's key and is never claimed. OpenCode keeps its data in the XDG data directory on every platform, so $XDG_DATA_HOME moves both files. Seen on opencode v2.0.32, Linux.

windows.notes: Same as macOS. Unverified on Windows; OpenCode may also use %APPDATA%/opencode. $XDG_DATA_HOME moves it here too.

linux.notes: Already the XDG data directory on every platform, so this is the macOS block unchanged. Confirmed on the maintainer's machine, opencode v2.0.32. $XDG_DATA_HOME moves it.

endpoints.name: usage
endpoints.notes: 401 with error.code = api_key_expired → rejected: the key expired and signing in again does not renew it (OpenCode's own message says so); the card says to create a new key in OpenCode Console and drops the last reading. Any other 401 → needsAuth (a missing Go plan and a bad key look the same upstream, body {"type":"error","error":{"type":"AuthError","message":"Unauthorized"}}). 403 → nothingMetered: a valid key without a Go subscription. Zen pay-as-you-go credit has no API at all.

windows.label: 5h limit
windows.notes: Fixed table driven by the client. A window without percent is dropped; no windows at all is a bad response, not zeros. Timestamps carry milliseconds.
